item.title: Merz makes surprise visit to Kyiv: Germany pledges further aid to Ukraine
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv on Sunday. Accompanied by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and representatives of German defence and energy companies, he aims to pledge further military and financial support for Ukraine.

item.title: Latvia's pro-European ruling party wins election as populists gain ground
item.description: With more than 99.9 per cent of votes counted, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' United List party was in the lead with 35.4 percent, according to state TV.

item.title: Off the Record: Teflon Rutte is on a mission to keep NATO together
item.description: Every week, Euronews' Chief Europe Editor Maria Tadeo breaks down the stories that made the week in Brussels and beyond. This week: her exclusive interview with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte — a man with Teflon skin.

item.title: Spanish police begin clearing Ceuta's largest migrant camp ahead of King and Queen's visit
item.description: Police began Operation Trampolín on Sunday to clear a makeshift settlement on Ceuta's Trampolín beach, home to about 3,000 people living in poor conditions for more than two months.

item.title: FlyDubai captain said he had “one more fight left in me” and opened cockpit door
item.description: FlyDubai hero captain Smit Machchhar described to Israeli prime minister Benjanim Netanyahu how the attack started and how he managed to finally open the cockpit door after nearly losing his vision under the co-pilot’s repeated blows.

item.title: 'I want to spark new ideas': Architect Ma Yansong on designing the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
item.description: Last month, film producer George Lucas opened his long-awaited Museum of Narrative Art for many legions of fans of Star Wars memorabilia and visual storytelling. Ma Yansong, the Chinese architect who designed the futuristic looking building, says he hopes it "sparks curiosity and new ideas."

item.title: North Korea fires intermediate-range missile, claiming evasive flight and AI features
item.description: Japan’s military said the missile landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone, while South Korea's military, which often accuses the North of exaggerating its capabilities, said it travelled more than 700 kilometres.

item.title: Bosnia votes as pro-Russian politician looms large over race and stalled EU bid dominate election
item.description: Around 3.4 million voters in Bosnia are choosing the three members of the country’s multi-ethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national Parliament, and heads of institutions for the country’s two entities.

item.title: Increasing influence: Italy marks 800 years since death of Saint Francis of Assisi
item.description: Ceremonies and events are being held in Assisi throughout the day in honour of Italy's patron saint. The festivities form part of the Franciscan Jubilee Year, proclaimed by Pope Leo XIV.

item.title: The eyes have it: Iconic World Cup pictures explored by Getty photographers
item.description: Whether on or off the pitch, many of the most memorable moments from FIFA World Cups have been captured by Getty. Here, some of the photographers behind those lenses share their thoughts about taking the best emotive images.

item.title: Shooting and scoring: Photographer Alex Pantling on capturing the world’s greatest footballers
item.description: Getty photographer Alex Pantling reported on the FIFA World Cup 2026 and shared with European Lens his reflection on the experience along with some of his favourite shots from the tournament.

item.title: Where is Europe’s greenest city? Eight finalists announced for 2028 and three are in Spain
item.description: The finalists were judged in seven areas, including climate change resilience, waste management and how quickly they are cutting emissions.

item.title: The best place to retire abroad is no longer in Europe – but six of the top ten are
item.description: European destinations scored highly in a new global retirement ranking, with six countries among the top ten, as people looking to retire abroad weigh higher taxes against quality of life.

item.title: Where to celebrate Halloween 2026 in Europe: Spooky cities, haunted hotels and scary events
item.description: Fancy a fright? These European destinations, hotels and Halloween events promise everything from Gothic legends to full-blown horror.

item.title: Researchers discover how the brain updates memories with new information
item.description: A joint study by three Spanish institutions shows how certain hippocampal neurons safeguard existing memories even as new information about events is stored.

item.title: Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan join forces in major military exercise
item.description: Thousands of military personnel from Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan, as well as other nations participating as observers, including Iran, joined forces in the “Power of Unity, 2026” military exercise for the first time, in the Hojavend district of Azerbaijan’s Karabakh region.

item.title: Tens of thousands take to Madrid streets demanding housing action
item.description: Tens of thousands of protesters marched through Madrid demanding affordable housing and stronger protections for renters, a day after lawmakers rejected emergency housing measures.

item.title: Brazil's Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro wrap up campaigns on eve of tight vote
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro have a final chance on Saturday to sway voters at rallies in crucial São Paulo before a tight election marked by scandals and personal attacks.

item.title: Tens of thousands of people take to streets of Paris to march for Pride
item.description: Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire, who leaded the march through the capital, highlighted some of the threats that the LGBTQ+ community is still facing, saying, "LGBTQIA+ venues are still being threatened, attacked, discriminated against, and subjected to violence and intimidation."

item.title: Ceuta support T-shirt: €10 of its €35 price goes to self-described ‘patriotic’ movement Save Europe Act
item.description: A T-shirt bearing the slogan “We are all from Ceuta” is being sold as a show of support for Ceuta, but part of the proceeds goes to Save Europe Act, a self-described patriotic movement that advocates remigration.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 3rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Nearly 500,000 people protest in Madrid over Spain's housing crisis
item.description: Thousands take to the streets across Spain as protesters call for a general strike after parliament rejects two government housing decrees.

item.title: IEA says 325 million barrels of emergency oil released, with 75 million still to come
item.description: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude after US pressure on Europe, with supplies squeezed by Iran's restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Showers and storms across Spain this weekend, floods kill 102-year-old woman
item.description: A 102-year-old woman has died and about 90 people were rescued in Madrigueras, Albacete, after floods dumped 142 l/m². Rain will persist, with a new storm possible in the west on Sunday.

item.title: Greece will not 'borrow' its own treasures, Mitsotakis says of Parthenon Marbles
item.description: Bulgaria's Rumen Radev said the two countries had left the shadows of the past behind them, and the 48 artefacts will go on display until 5 November before returning to the places they were taken from.

item.title: Azerbaijan International Investment Forum: Where capital meets opportunity
item.description: The 2nd Azerbaijan International Investment Forum brought together representatives from more than 70 countries to discuss investment, trade, infrastructure and diversification, with more than $10 billion in contracts and agreements signed.

item.title: Germany marks 36 years of unity: Why was the country divided and how united is it today?
item.description: Only 17% of former GDR citizens kept their jobs after the change of system, a legacy still visible in regions short of people and corporate headquarters.

item.title: Seventeen EU leaders press Irish presidency to protect farm funding in next budget
item.description: With Giorgia Meloni and Nicușor Dan as first signatories, the group also wants cohesion funding preserved, national rebates scrapped and NextGenerationEU loan repaid more slowly to free up fiscal space.

item.title: China opens anti-dumping probe into EU days before Beijing trade talks
item.description: Running a €1 billion-a-day deficit with China, Brussels has nearly tripled the rate of its own trade investigations and is warning of "harsher measures" unless Beijing offers something concrete.

item.title: UAE says FlyDubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe in 'terrorist' act
item.description: The FlyDubai co-pilot who nearly crashed the Tel-Aviv bound flight is an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami. He was barred from flying by Oman amid concerns he showed signs of extremist views. The incident threw the already hard-hit regional travel industry into crisis.

item.title: Spain faces housing protests in more than 50 cities after parliament rejects tenant protections
item.description: The eviction of an 87-year-old woman has turned anger over rents that have nearly doubled in ten years into a threat to Pedro Sánchez's minority government.

item.title: Latvia: Exit polls show ruling party leading as populist party gains momentum
item.description: Some 1.5 million people were eligible to cast their ballots in the Saturday parliamentary election, Latvia's 11th since gaining independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.

item.title: Second Kyiv bridge hit in two days as Russia targets Dnipro crossings
item.description: With the Northern Bridge's traffic blocked a day after jet-powered drones forced the Southern Bridge shut, two of the eight Dnipro crossings joining Kyiv's halves are now disrupted.

item.title: The way you speak could reveal early signs of brain ageing
item.description: The way we speak may reveal how quickly we are ageing, with older-sounding speech linked to dementia and brain changes.

item.title: Hungarian restaurants struggle: costs match Europe but revenues lag behind
item.description: A new study says tourist traps create competition that squeezes quality restaurants, as foreign visitor numbers fall and most Hungarians cannot afford to eat out regularly.

item.title: The Disney generation: What unites Baby Boomers, millennials and Gen Z
item.description: Disney stories may be aimed at children, but their lessons can last a lifetime. A study by SWPS University in Poland found that values such as friendship, loyalty, family, courage, resilience and being yourself can stay with us well into adulthood.

item.title: ‘It’s given my mental health a massive boost’: Why everyone should hone their bushcraft skills
item.description: The Bushcraft Bus is reconnecting Europeans with nature.

item.title: House prices keep rising across Europe: Which countries saw the biggest increases and why?
item.description: House prices in Europe continue to rise, outpacing inflation in many countries. Annual increases ranged from 0.6% in Germany to 16.5% in Portugal in the second quarter of 2026.

item.title: From food-led escapes to trip of a lifetime hotels: How luxury travel has evolved and ‘doesn’t look one way’
item.description: The fusion of food and hospitality is a major driving force in the world of luxury travel. We spoke to Michelin Guide's Marie-France Perrel about how the sector is changing.

item.title: Russia leads world in cat ownership — yet has 2.8 million strays
item.description: Nearly 59% of Russian households own at least one cat, the highest rate globally, but the 2022 mobilisation order left hundreds of thousands of animals abandoned when owners fled the country or were sent to the front in Ukraine. Up to 98% of Russia's stray cats and dogs were once domestic pets.

item.title: Tension rises in Ceuta: two migrant children stabbed and bacteria-contaminated beach
item.description: Two migrant children were stabbed in a knife attack in Ceuta, while health authorities have found high levels of bacteria in the water at Trampolín beach, near a migrant camp. The migration crisis is forcing some people to sleep in garages, vehicles and on rooftops.

item.title: US suspends consular services in Brazil as Lula and Bolsonaro fight for election
item.description: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and rival Flavio Bolsonaro are pulling no punches in a last-ditch effort to win voters ahead of Sunday's election in Brazil, where the US and Australia suspended consular services Friday over security concerns.

item.title: Sánchez begins reflection on early election as protesters call for general strike
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister will decide this weekend whether to call early elections after his two housing decrees were rejected, as housing activists prepare fresh protests and consider a general strike as the next step.

item.title: Russia 'tearing Kyiv apart', mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
item.description: Russian attacks on key infrastructure were "tearing Kyiv apart", the city's mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital's east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

item.title: Debt-saddled Argentina pitches 'golden passport' scheme to woo wealthy foreigners
item.description: Argentina on Friday announced plans to offer citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for cash contributions or investments in government bonds, as libertarian President Javier Milei seeks new sources of dollars for the debt-burdened nation.

item.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak killed more than 4,000: official figures
item.description: The worst ever Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now killed more than 4,000 people out of more than 8,000 confirmed cases, Congolese officials said on Friday.
